steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A breadboard provides a solderless prototyping platform with internal spring contacts connecting rows and columns.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Breadboard connections are temporary and suitable for testing circuit designs before permanent construction.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Stripboard (Veroboard) has copper tracks in rows; tracks must be cut to isolate sections where connections are not wanted.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: PCB design involves creating a layout with copper tracks that connect component pads according to the circuit schematic.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Describe the difference between a breadboard and a stripboard. | Q: What are two PCB design rules that must be followed? | Q: Describe the steps to create a good solder joint.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A breadboard is solderless and used for temporary prototyping with spring contacts; stripboard has copper tracks and requires soldering for permanent connections. | Tracks must be wide enough to carry the required current, and there must be sufficient clearance between adjacent tracks to prevent short circuits. | Clean the tip, apply iron to heat both pad and lead simultaneously, feed solder onto the joint, remove solder, then remove the iron; the joint should be shiny and concave.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When describing soldering, always mention heating both the pad and the lead before applying solder. List at least three PCB design rules: track width, clearance, pad size, component orientation. Know the visual difference: a good joint is shiny and concave; a dry joint is dull and granular. For breadboard questions, explain the internal connections (rows linked, columns linked for power rails). Mention the purpose of a solder mask and silk screen layer when describing PCB construction.
